_: Written from the field table in harness/README.md, not copied from an example. Every number here is either derived from this run's own interview answers or a first guess that the tiny proof is allowed to overrule.
_topics: The harness owns the orders topic and the two position topics, and nothing else. prices is a second INPUT: this run creates it, fills it and reads it, and it appears in neither list. The two market-value topics are throttled outputs -- their rows are per 10-second interval, not per order -- so they stay out of topics.out and are declared below instead.
_design: What the interview asked for, as lists the completeness step can diff against the running job. Question 1 asks for two position outputs and a market value against each of them, so there are two market values, not one.
_outputsPerInput: Derived from this run's own answer to question 2: every order carries exactly 4 allocations, so it writes 1 row to positions-by-symbol and 4 to positions-by-account. 1 + 4 = 5. The two market values are emitted on a timer and are deliberately not in this number.
_backlog: First guesses. This run has measured nothing yet, so these are sized from a deliberately high assumption of 500,000 orders a second at the 4-core case: the suite needs (240 warm-up + 70 window + 20 checkpoint) seconds of it and the tiny proof (120 + 40 + 20). The tiny proof measures the real rate and the harness says what to use instead. smallCount has to span several checkpoint intervals at the ONE-core rate so the kill can land where it is asked to.
_caps: The virtual machine is 9,937 MiB. At the 4-core case the worker asks for 1024 + 4 x 640 = 3,584m, the job manager takes 1,600m, and that leaves about 4,700m for the broker. kafkaMemory minus kafkaHeap is what the broker caches the backlog with: 4,608m less 1G is about 3.5 GB. The shipped example's 6g broker plus a 4-core worker would be 11,392m on a 9,937 MiB machine, which is the configuration the skill's own run 45 measured the worker giving way under.
_flinkProperties: The garbage collector is pinned because --cpus 1 makes the JVM see one processor and pick the serial collector, which would make the baseline a different program from every other case. The Prometheus reporter is what five of the dashboard's seven panels need; on flink:1.20.x the reporter jars are already installed as plugins, so nothing else is required and ENABLE_BUILT_IN_PLUGINS must NOT be set. pipeline.max-parallelism is filled in from what the key-layout preflight row names, before the stack is brought up for the chain.
_keySets: The manifest fields holding each keyed stage's keys, so preflight can ask Flink's own key-group assignment where 4 symbols and 16 account keys would land at 1, 2 and 4 subtasks.
_extraServices: Section 7's dashboard, in the compose file so that teardown reaps it, every container named for the project, and every one capped: anything sharing the cores under test changes the number being measured. The exporter directory is mounted, not the file, because a tool that rewrites the file replaces the inode.
axis: one worker growing: one task manager container capped at N cores, parallelism N, N slots
apiLevel: Flink DataStream API, hand-written operators (no SQL, no Table API)

guarantee.sink: at-least-once, idempotent by publishing the absolute position per key
